records.title: [v0.92.2][Runtime] Teach admitted agents about Polis modules and capabilities
records.body:
## Summary

Expand the versioned Axioma Polis Welcome Package so every admitted agent receives a truthful orientation to the Polis modules, capabilities, governance boundaries, and discovery surfaces available to it. The current package describes general governance but does not explicitly teach agents about Freedom Gate or provide a usable map of the broader Runtime.

## Goal

Make newly admitted agents understand where they are, which Polis modules and capabilities exist, how those capabilities are used through governed Runtime contracts, and how to determine what is actually enabled for their identity and deployment.

## Required Outcome

The standard versioned welcome package delivered to every admitted agent contains a source-grounded Polis capability orientation covering the Runtime's current module families and operational capabilities, including Freedom Gate. It must distinguish platform capability from agent authority and deployment availability, and remain synchronized with the Runtime's canonical capability/module inventory.

## Deliverables

- A revised, versioned Axioma Polis Welcome Package with an agent-readable map of the Polis.
- Orientation covering identity and offices, provider-backed reasoning, ACIP/Layer 8 agent communication, UTS and ACC governed tool use, Freedom Gate, AEE, checkpoints/partials and continuity, memory and observability, Shepherd coordination, scheduling/time services, and operator escalation.
- A clear explanation that agents use modules through admitted Runtime capabilities and contracts rather than calling internal Rust modules directly.
- A Runtime-derived or validated module/capability inventory that prevents stale or invented orientation claims.
- Delivery through the versioned orientation resource introduced by #708, preserving per-agent version and digest provenance.
- Focused documentation, Runtime, API/read-model, and Observatory contract tests as applicable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every newly admitted agent receives the expanded orientation before its first model turn through the existing versioned welcome-package path.
- The package explicitly explains Freedom Gate as the pre-execution decision boundary that may allow, constrain, defer, or refuse a proposed action.
- The package describes every canonical Polis module family and externally meaningful capability represented by the Runtime's authoritative registries, with concise guidance on what it does and how an agent uses it.
- The package distinguishes capability existence, deployment enablement, agent admission, and per-action authorization.
- The package states that orientation grants no authority and cannot override Runtime policy, admission, Freedom Gate, Layer 8, operator authority, privacy rules, or provider availability.
- Agents are told how to inspect or request their effective capabilities and how to ask the Shepherd or operator when availability or authority is unclear.
- A deterministic guard compares the orientation inventory with the canonical Runtime inventory and fails on missing, stale, or invented entries.
- Existing agents retain the orientation version/digest they received; newly admitted agents receive the active valid version, consistent with #708.
- Observatory/API provenance continues to expose the exact welcome-package version and digest delivered to each agent.
- Focused tests prove first-turn delivery, Freedom Gate coverage, inventory coverage, deployment-aware wording, non-authority language, and stale-inventory detection without live provider or cloud use.

## Repo Inputs

- `docs/runtime/AXIOMA_POLIS_WELCOME_PACKAGE_V1.md`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/agent_orientation.rs`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/control.rs`
- Runtime component factories, service contracts, capability registries, API/read-model projections, and Observatory presentation.
- `docs/GLOSSARY.md`
- `docs/architecture/RUNTIME_V3_OPERATIONAL_COMPONENTS.md`
- `docs/explainers/ACIP.md`
- `docs/explainers/UTS_AND_ACC.md`
- Issue #708 and PR #709.

## Dependencies

- Builds on completed issue #708 / PR #709.
- Allocate to v0.92.2 when that GitHub milestone is opened.

## Demo Expectations

A deterministic local demonstration admits a test agent, captures its initial model context and orientation receipt, and proves it can identify Freedom Gate, the major available capability families, the difference between availability and authority, and the governed path for using or requesting a capability.

## Non-goals

- Granting agents new authority, tools, communication rights, or autonomy.
- Exposing credentials, private policy content, or unnecessary implementation details.
- Replacing canonical Runtime registries with prose as the source of truth.
- Requiring every deployment or agent to enable every platform capability.
- Changing Freedom Gate, ACIP, UTS, ACC, AEE, continuity, provider, or scheduling behavior.
- Live provider calls, cloud changes, or production Runtime mutation.

## Issue-Graph Notes

This is a v0.92.2 follow-up to #708. It extends orientation content and inventory validation; it does not reopen or replace the completed delivery mechanism.

## Notes

Keep the package concise enough to function as model context. Prefer a compact capability map plus effective-capability discovery over exhaustive implementation documentation. Names and descriptions must be source-grounded and deployment-aware.

## Tooling Notes

Use the active typed C-SDLC lifecycle. Work only in a bound FastWork issue worktree, keep primary `main` inspection-only, use focused docs/Runtime contract validation, and obtain fresh exact-head review before publication.

records.title: [v0.92.2][Runtime] Route agent-to-agent communication by canonical agent name
records.body:
## Summary

Change Runtime agent-to-agent addressing so agents address peers by canonical agent identity names such as `ember.axioma`, rather than implementation-facing admission or model-derived IDs such as `gemma-e4b`.

## Goal

Make A2A communication stable across model replacement, provider changes, migration, checkpoint restoration, and node placement.

## Required Outcome

The public agent communication contract accepts a canonical agent name, resolves it through the authoritative live roster, and keeps internal IDs, provider details, model IDs, and physical routing metadata private to Runtime.

## Deliverables

- Replace the public `recipient_id` A2A tool argument with a canonical-name recipient contract.
- Resolve canonical names to immutable internal agent identity and delivery routes inside Runtime.
- Update agent prompts and the welcome package so agents discover and address peers by canonical name.
- Preserve internal identifiers for persistence, audit, replay, migration, and compatibility without exposing them as peer addresses.
- Add API/schema, Runtime, ACIP/A2A, history, and Observatory projection tests.
- Define a bounded compatibility path for retained records or clients that still contain legacy recipient IDs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Any admitted agent can initiate a governed A2A message using a canonical name such as `ember.axioma`.
- Runtime rejects missing, malformed, self-targeted, unknown, or ambiguous canonical names with explicit errors.
- Replacing an agent's model or provider does not change its A2A address.
- Migrating, freeze-drying, and rehydrating an agent preserves its canonical A2A identity.
- Provider prompts and tool schemas do not instruct agents to use model IDs or deployment IDs.
- Observable A2A history records both canonical sender and recipient names while retaining correlated internal audit identity.
- Focused end-to-end proof shows at least two non-Shepherd agents addressing one another by canonical name and receiving model-generated replies.

## Repo Inputs

- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/assembly.rs`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/control.rs`
- `adl-runtime-kernel/src/ingress.rs`
- Runtime agent roster and admission identity contracts
- ACIP A2A carrier contracts
- Observatory A2A history projections
- `docs/runtime/AXIOMA_POLIS_WELCOME_PACKAGE_V1.md`

## Dependencies

- Builds on the existing governed A2A initiation and canonical agent naming work.
- Target release: v0.92.2.

## Demo Expectations

From the Observatory, instruct one ordinary resident agent to contact another using only the recipient's canonical name. Show the complete outbound message, governed delivery, recipient model execution, reply, and durable history without exposing model IDs as addresses.

## Non-goals

- Changing an agent's backing model or provider.
- Introducing Shepherd-specific communication rules.
- Designing distributed cross-node transport beyond preserving the name-to-route abstraction.
- Replacing ACIP or weakening signed-message validation.

## Issue-Graph Notes

Unassigned v0.92.2 backlog issue. It should remain independently executable and must not block current milestone startup.

## Notes

Canonical names are identities such as `ember.axioma`; display labels such as `Ember Axioma` are presentation, and model names such as `gemma4:e4b-mlx` are replaceable implementation details. Name uniqueness and normalization must be enforced at admission so routing is deterministic.

## Tooling Notes

Use the typed C-SDLC lifecycle. Validate the public schema and observable end-to-end behavior; helper-only tests are not sufficient.

<!-- csdlc-github-operation:v0922-runtime-a2a-canonical-name-routing -->

records.title: [v0.92.2][Observatory] Remove retained-mode demo hazards
records.body:
## Goal

Make the production/live Observatory fail-safe for demonstrations by removing one-click paths that silently replace live Runtime v3 telemetry with frozen retained-packet data.

## Required outcome

- Remove the Published and Retained topbar modes from the live Observatory and pin the product surface to Live.
- Remove or isolate refreshRetained and its three-second static-file polling so the live build cannot continuously fetch v0.91.7 retained JSON.
- Remove the orphaned setRuntimeTestStatus local assignments currently reported near app.js lines 3293, 4298, and 4371.
- Preserve historical retained artifacts as repository evidence; do not delete evidence merely to hide it from the product UI.
- Ensure the live UI cannot silently present historical/frozen data as current polis telemetry.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The live Observatory offers no Published or Retained mode controls.
2. Normal startup and navigation cannot replace live telemetry with docs/milestones/v0.91.7/review/runtime/csm_liveness_4976/published/api data.
3. No obsolete three-second retained refresh timer runs in the live product path.
4. The three unused status assignments are removed.
5. Focused tests prove Live remains functional and no retained-mode route is reachable from the live UI.
6. Documentation distinguishes retained historical evidence from the live Observatory product.

## Non-goals

- Do not delete immutable v0.91.7 evidence.
- Do not redesign the Observatory.
- Do not widen issue #512 or delay its publication.

## Scheduling

Target v0.92.2. The v0.92.2 milestone is not yet open, so attach this issue when that milestone is created.

records.title: [v0.92.2][planning] Audit and refresh first-pass milestone documentation
records.body:
## Outcome

Produce a reviewed first-pass v0.92.2 planning package that is coherent, execution-oriented, and ready for later milestone opening without claiming that v0.92.2 is open or approved.

## Existing baseline

The repository already contains a candidate package under `docs/milestones/v0.92.2/`, including the core milestone documents, two machine-readable work-wave files, and first-class CodeFriend Beta 1 feature documents. This issue audits and refreshes that package rather than recreating it.

## Scope

- Reconcile the complete canonical v0.92.2 document inventory.
- Align vision, design, decisions, WBS, sprint plan, planned issue catalog, issue wave, execution specifications, readiness, quality gate, demo matrix, checklist, release surfaces, ADR plan, successor handoff, and feature documents.
- Keep the package number-free and in planned posture until the operator opens the milestone.
- Make every planned issue a single bounded unit of work with a concrete result, explicit dependencies, owned deliverables, and proving validation.
- Reconcile CodeFriend Beta 1 against its source planning and ensure shell, adapter, evidence, cognition, governance, review, memory, publication, proof, and integration tracks are complete without scope inflation.
- Audit active `.adl/docs/TBD/` material against the milestone package and local backlog. Classify every relevant source as v0.92.2 candidate, later milestone, explicit backlog/deferred work, operational reference, completed provenance, or unresolved scheduling gap.
- Record unplanned or unscheduled material in a bounded disposition table; do not silently pull it into v0.92.2.
- Cross-check existing open issues and later-milestone routing so the package neither duplicates work nor loses previously scheduled work.

## Required deliverables

- Refreshed full planning package under `docs/milestones/v0.92.2/`.
- Updated canonical document inventory and feature index.
- Findings-first TBD scheduling reconciliation with source path, current status, proposed home, rationale, and unresolved decision.
- Machine-valid `WP_ISSUE_WAVE_v0.92.2.yaml` and `WP_EXECUTION_SPECIFICATIONS_v0.92.2.yaml`.
- Focused package validator covering inventory, YAML, relative links, placeholders, number-free issue planning, exact release-tail structure, and TBD disposition completeness.
- Review handoff stating what changed, what remains deferred, what needs operator decision, and what must happen before WP-01 may be created.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every canonical planning document exists and agrees on milestone purpose, scope, dependencies, sequencing, and planned posture.
- [ ] Every first-class work track has a feature document, WBS/WP home, proof expectation, and release/readiness disposition.
- [ ] Every planned issue represents one bounded unit of work with a concrete deliverable and acceptance denominator.
- [ ] The number-free issue catalog, issue-wave YAML, execution specifications, readiness table, and sprint plan agree exactly.
- [ ] The ten-step release tail is consistent across all planning surfaces.
- [ ] Active TBD documents relevant to future product, Runtime, provider, workflow, demo, cloud, documentation, or architecture work are inventoried and assigned a truthful disposition.
- [ ] Unplanned or unscheduled TBD material is explicitly listed; backlog and later-milestone work remains deferred rather than being silently scheduled.
- [ ] Existing issues and completed work are reconciled so the package does not duplicate or reopen delivered scope.
- [ ] Markdown links resolve, YAML parses, machine-local paths and unresolved placeholders are rejected, and `git diff --check` passes.
- [ ] A bounded independent review has no unresolved actionable finding before PR publication.

## Dependencies and opening boundary

- v0.92.1 remains the active milestone.
- This issue may prepare v0.92.2 documentation in parallel but must not open the v0.92.2 milestone, create WP-01 or child implementation issues, or move live issues before the operator explicitly authorizes milestone opening.
- Current v0.92.1 release-tail truth must be reflected as a dependency, not treated as documentation closeout work for this issue.

## Non-goals

- Opening the v0.92.2 GitHub milestone or creating a `version:v0.92.2` label.
- Creating WP-01, sprint umbrellas, or child implementation issues.
- Implementing CodeFriend Beta 1 or any other product feature.
- Pulling Unity, ATE, MLX/Metal, OCI packaging, cloud migrations, broad integrations, or Runtime v4 into v0.92.2 without explicit operator direction.
- Editing or deleting `.adl/docs/TBD/` source material merely to make the inventory clean.
- Broad Rust/runtime testing for a documentation-only change.

## Focused validation

- Canonical planning-document inventory check.
- YAML parsing and cross-file WP identity/dependency parity.
- Relative Markdown link resolution.
- Scoped placeholder, absolute-path, duplicate-ID, and stale-version scan.
- TBD source/disposition coverage check.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`.

## Owned paths

- `docs/milestones/v0.92.2/**`
- `.csdlc/issues/620/**`
- `.csdlc/prepared/issues/620/**`

The implementation PR must use `Closes #620`.
